bl_007.name: Model
bl_007.doc: Title, purpose, viewpoint; diagrams; the concept registry.

bl_006.name: Diagram
bl_006.doc: A-0 context, or a decomposition of a box: one landscape sheet, a node number.

bl_003.name: Box
bl_003.doc: An activity: a verb phrase, a box number 0–6, bound to a concept. May be decomposed into a child diagram, or call another.

bl_001.name: Arrow
bl_001.doc: Input, control, output or mechanism (ICOM); a noun-phrase label bound to a concept; forks, joins, tunnels.

bl_005.name: Concept
bl_005.doc: The identity behind every name and label. Renaming carries every occurrence; renaming onto an existing term merges.

bl_004.name: Bundle
bl_004.doc: A concept that combines others, in order. Un-combining is lossless.

bl_002.name: Boundary port
bl_002.doc: I1, C1, O1, M1… — a child’s inherited boundary arrow keeps its parent’s conceptId.

bl_018.name: IDEF0 Modeler (web)
bl_018.doc: Served by ./serve.sh at :8123, or by the Portal at /idef0/.

bl_028.name: Persistence
bl_028.doc: Asks the browser to keep this app’s data, and reports whether it agreed.

bl_025.name: Model operations
bl_025.doc: model.js — structure, decomposition, staircase layout, node numbering, ICOM codes, ports, bundles.

bl_024.name: Geometry
bl_024.doc: Anchor resolution, rectilinear routing, port shapes.

bl_026.name: Naming edits
bl_026.doc: edits.js — rename a box, label an arrow, as model operations.

bl_027.name: Rule checker
bl_027.doc: validate.js — every code a stable identifier shared by the web panel, the Mac panel and idef0 validate --json.

bl_032.name: Renderer
bl_032.doc: render.js — used unchanged by the exporters: what you see is what lands in the SVG, PNG and PDF.

bl_030.name: Canvas
bl_030.doc: Hit testing, arrow and port drags, drawing, pan and zoom.

bl_031.name: Panels
bl_031.doc: Node tree, model properties, glossary, inspector, checks.

bl_021.name: Report
bl_021.doc: Node index, activity and arrow tables, glossary, rule-check results; IDL listing.

bl_019.name: Image export
bl_019.doc: SVG, PNG, PDF (the diagram or the whole kit).

bl_010.name: IDEF0 Modeler.app
bl_010.doc: SwiftUI DocumentGroup: must run as a real .app bundle, which reads its document types from Info.plist.

bl_008.name: idef0 CLI
bl_008.doc: Checks, converts, reports on and renders a model without opening either app.

bl_009.name: Swift core
bl_009.doc: Same .idef0.json, same XML, same rule checker, the same message text.

bl_011.name: Golden fixtures
bl_011.doc: Captured headlessly from the web modules (golden-harness.js); the Swift tests compare against them, and goldens-staleness fails when they lag the web code.

bl_016.name: ui-kit
bl_016.doc: The shared HUD: tokens, CSS, theme runtime, web components.

bl_014.name: sync-kit
bl_014.doc: The record-sync client: SyncEngine, a store, HttpTransport.

bl_015.doc: Collects the app from toolkit-app.json and serves it at /idef0/ on one origin.

bl_012.name: Ontology toolkit
bl_012.doc: Downstream tools that read the model: the concept registry and idef0 --json.

us_003.name: Decompose an activity
us_003.doc: 3–6 boxes; boundary arrows inherited with their concepts.

us_002.name: Curate the glossary
us_002.doc: Rename, merge, bundle and un-bundle concepts.

us_006.name: Publish the kit
us_006.doc: SVG, PNG, PDF, report, IDL, XML.

re_002.name: FIPS 183 syntax
re_002.text: A-0 shall hold exactly one box; a decomposition 3–6; every box a control and an output; every arrow a label.

re_001.name: Every name is a concept
re_001.text: Every named box and labelled arrow shall be bound to a glossary concept.

re_004.name: Stable rule codes
re_004.text: Every finding shall carry a code shared by the web panel, the Mac panel and idef0 validate --json.

re_006.name: Web and Swift agree
re_006.text: The Swift port shall read, write and check a model byte for byte as the web modules do.

re_005.name: Times are never invented
re_005.text: An element with no updatedAt or deletedAt shall be written back with none, so an older file saves byte for byte.

re_003.name: Screen equals export
re_003.text: What is drawn on screen shall be exactly what lands in the SVG, PNG and PDF.
